title: DNA Extraction from Sterivex Filters
author: Christopher Neil Thornton
materials: Gently shake a few times and centrifuge.
Invert a few times to mix.

steps.title: Prepare DNA Extraction Buffer (DEB)
steps.instruction: Combine the following reagents in a 50 mL tube: 0.1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 8), 4.5 mL of 1.0 M Na‑EDTA (pH 8), 9 mL of 0.5 M KH₂PO₄ (pH 8), 0.54 g of 1.5 M NaCl, 13.5 mL of 5 M Guanidine‑HCl, 3.44 g of 0.8 M Guanidine‑HCl, 225 µL (0.5 %) Triton‑X‑100. Add Milli‑Q water to approximately 40 mL, adjust pH to 10 with a few drops of NaOH, then bring volume to 45 mL with Milli‑Q water. Filter‑sterilize, autoclave with the lid loosely closed, recover the solution immediately after the cycle, aliquot into 1.5 mL tubes and store.

substeps.instruction: Add Tris‑HCl, Na‑EDTA, KH₂PO₄, NaCl, Guanidine‑HCl, and Triton‑X‑100 to a 50 mL tube.
Adjust pH to 10 with NaOH (few drops).
Recover quickly, aliquot into 1.5 mL tubes.

steps.title: Add DEB to Sterivex Filters
steps.instruction: Using a syringe and needle, add 1.4 mL of the prepared DEB to each Sterivex filter; position the needle just below the filter mouth so it does not exit the top, and stop when the solution fully covers the white filter. Optionally store the filter at –20 °C.

steps.title: Place Sterivex in Perforated Tube
steps.instruction: Insert each Sterivex filter into a 50 mL tube that has holes (perforated tube).

steps.title: Incubate Sterivex at 65 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube containing the Sterivex at 65 °C for 30 minutes on a Genemate spinning machine.

steps.title: Vortex Sterivex for Bead Beating
steps.instruction: Vortex the Sterivex (still inside the Falcon tube) for 30 seconds to perform bead beating.

steps.title: Transfer Lysate to Bead Tube
steps.instruction: Using a syringe, withdraw the lysate from each Sterivex and eject it into a bead tube containing 0.1 mm glass beads for bacteria.

steps.title: Centrifuge Bead Tube
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the bead tube for 2 minutes at 5,000 g.

steps.title: Collect Supernatant into Fresh Tubes
steps.instruction: Transfer the cleared fluid (avoiding beads) into a fresh Eppendorf tube; add no more than 900 µL per tube (or ≤750 µL if using 1.5 mL tubes).

steps.title: Mix and Spin High‑Speed
steps.instruction: Gently shake the tube a few times, then centrifuge for 1 minute at 14,000 g.

steps.title: Transfer Supernatant to New Tubes
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant and place it into a fresh tube.

steps.title: Add Phenol‑Chloroform‑Isoamyl Alcohol
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of phenol : chloroform : isoamyl alcohol (25 : 24 : 1, pre‑mixed with alkaline buffer) to each tube and mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Add Chloroform‑Isoamyl Alcohol
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of chloroform : isoamyl alcohol (24 : 1) to each tube and mix.

steps.title: Collect Aqueous Phase
steps.instruction: Carefully remove the upper aqueous layer to a fresh tube, avoiding the bottom organic layer.

steps.title: Redistribute Aqueous Phase into Small Tubes
steps.instruction: Divide the aqueous phase among up to three tubes so that each 2.0 mL tube receives ≤550 µL (or ≤450 µL for 1.6 mL tubes). If sodium acetate is omitted, a maximum of 600 µL can be placed in a 2.0 mL tube.

steps.title: Add Sodium Acetate
steps.instruction: Add 0.1 volumes of 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.2) to each tube (e.g., 55 µL to 550 µL).

steps.title: Add Ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 2 volumes of 100 % ethanol to each tube (e.g., 1,210 µL to 605 µL).

steps.title: Add Glycogen (optional)
steps.instruction: For low‑biomass samples, add 1.2 µL of glycogen (20 µg/µL).

steps.title: Precipitate DNA at –20 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture at –20 °C for at least 1 hour or overnight; incubation on ice is an acceptable alternative.

steps.title: Pellet DNA by High‑Speed Spin
steps.instruction: Centrifuge for 40 minutes at 16,000 g (optional: use a refrigerated centrifuge at 0 °C).

steps.title: Discard Supernatant Carefully
steps.instruction: Pour out the supernatant while keeping the tube at a gentle angle to avoid dislodging the pellet.

steps.title: Wash Pellet with Cold 70 % Ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of cold 70 % ethanol to each tube.

steps.title: Resuspend Pellet and Centrifuge
steps.instruction: Invert the tube to mix, ensuring the pellet is fully dislodged, then centrifuge at 16,000 g for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Remove Ethanol Wash
steps.instruction: Remove the ethanol liquid with a pipettor, taking care not to disturb the pellet.

steps.title: Vacuum‑Dry Pellet
steps.instruction: Place open‑lid tubes in a Vacufuge and spin for 7 minutes at 30 °C (V‑AL setting). If ethanol remains, spin an additional 2–5 minutes; stop if pellets become powdery (over‑dry).

steps.title: Resuspend DNA in Low‑EDTA TE
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried pellet in ~100 µL of low‑EDTA TE buffer and heat at 55 °C until fully dissolved.

substeps.instruction: Prepare low‑EDTA TE (10 mM Tris‑HCl, 0.1 mM EDTA): for 50 mL, mix 500 µL of 1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 8.0) and 10 µL of 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0) with Milli‑Q water to 50 mL, then filter‑sterilize (0.22 µm).
Add ~100 µL of this buffer to the pellet.
Heat at 55 °C until the pellet dissolves.
